questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an English-speaking country because I wanted to be able to speak with the population. Moreover, I wanted to be more advanced in English, wherefore I chose Australia as my destination.

Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Were easy - we had a great supervisor Jane

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information about which dates to attend uni. how to chose and change units, when the exams would be held etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived at Queen Mary building, but the uni also cooperated with Scape.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Communal kitchen for all residents at Queen Mary Building.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Great for making new friends. Many people live together which can be hectic at some times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to change units and classes to make your timetable.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We couldn't see all courses we were able to apply for initially, wherefore I chose 2 other courses after my arrival in Sydney.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Jane our supervisor - and she was great.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help when needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Too many students weren't able to speak proper English. As we had lots of group assignments which influenced my work negatively.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was lower than in Denmark. However, there were many assignments that I needed to hand in all the time. The level of the assignments was also lower than in Denmark, probably because people, including myself, did not have time to make them as great as possible.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: USYD also had TAs and a lot of group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
IDEA9105	Interface Design

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

questions.answer: Everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to food bazars and to the lunches. They are great fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel, go to the museum, go to the beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the introduction activities at the uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of international students who could not speak English at the uni made it harder to get friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The events the uni held every day with food, shows, dogs visiting etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Familiarize yourself with the academic system of the host institution. Understand the course structure, grading system, and any unique academic expectations.


Actively engage with both local and international students.

Attend orientation events and workshops organized by the host institution to connect with fellow students and gain insights into the campus culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was undoubtedly the friendships I formed and the significant improvement in my language skills. Building connections with both local and international students enriched my time abroad in ways I hadn't anticipated. These friendships not only provided a support system but also allowed for a deeper cultural exchange, exposing me to different perspectives and traditions.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating unexpected expenses and finding that the overall cost was higher than anticipated became a significant challenge during my exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
